name: Meat-and-fruit diet

lead: The meat-and-fruit diet limits food mostly to meat (sometimes organ meats and dairy) and fruit. Followers use it to keep body fat low, to gain muscle on a high-protein base, and for the skin and energy changes they attribute to cutting processed food and most plants.

It is closely tied to the animal-based diet popularised by physician and podcaster Paul Saladino, who moved from strict carnivore eating to adding fruit and honey. Experts have criticised several of his health claims, and no trials have tested the pattern as such.

paras: People build meals around beef, other meats and sometimes eggs and organ meats, with fruit supplying carbohydrate. Some variants add honey and raw dairy. It is usually followed as a long-term lifestyle rather than a timed programme.

Commentators note it excludes vegetables, grains and legumes and is restrictive. Saladino reported sleep disturbance, heart palpitations, cramps and lower testosterone on strict carnivore eating before adding carbohydrate. Raw dairy, which some versions include, has drawn public-health concern.

angle.text: Followers say a protein-dense, minimally processed diet helps them hold less body fat while training. Skin and energy improvements are also claimed.

lead: The meat-and-fruit diet is an eating pattern consisting mainly of animal foods and fruit. It is discussed in fitness and looksmaxxing circles as a way to stay lean, support muscle and, as followers see it, improve skin and energy by dropping most plant foods and processed products.

It is most associated with Paul Saladino, a physician who was vegan before becoming a prominent carnivore advocate, appeared on Joe Rogan's podcast in 2020 and published The Carnivore Code that year. He reported side effects on strict carnivore eating, including sleep disturbance, palpitations, cramps and lower testosterone, and by 2020 had added carbohydrate in the form of fruit and honey, later promoting a meat-heavy diet with organ meats and raw dairy [1].
Experts have criticised his claims. Science communicator Joseph Schwarcz argued that he exaggerates risks drawn from studies [1]. No clinical trial has tested a meat-and-fruit diet specifically.
infobox: Meat (including organs), fruit, sometimes honey and dairy

paras: The pattern grew out of the carnivore-diet movement. Saladino said strict carnivore eating cured his anxiety and eczema, then reported that long-term ketosis might not suit him and added fruit and honey [1]. His 2020 Joe Rogan appearance expanded his audience [1].

Schwarcz said that fearmongering has become an industry and that Saladino exaggerates risks from studies; a New Republic writer called him a pseudoscience health influencer [1]. No trial of a diet limited to meat and fruit has been published.

Saladino reported sleep disturbances, heart palpitations, muscle cramps and lower testosterone on strict carnivore eating [1]. In 2024 he posted a video promoting raw dairy for infants and removed it the next day after backlash [1].

timeline.event: Saladino appears on Joe Rogan's podcast and publishes The Carnivore Code; he adds fruit and honey to his diet around this time [1].
Visits the Hadza in Tanzania, promoting their diet as a model [1].
